clue.text: Area of water par excellence

definitions.meaning: one of the North American Great Lakes, the largest of them
better than the rest, of the highest quality

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a great North American lake and the quality of being better than others.

clue.text: Society is mad to stir up enjoyment of cruelty

indicators.note: stirring up mixes the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Society is driven mad by those who stir up delight in cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stir up' rearranges IS MAD into ADISM, placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is pleasure taken in inflicting pain on others, named after the Marquis de Sade.

clue.text: Although a drudge, I could be loaded

definitions.text: Although a drudge, I could be loaded

parts.words: Although a drudge, I could be loaded
parts.note: a toiling animal speaking: though a lowly drudge it might be loaded, as if with money, but really with a burden of goods on its back

explanation.definitionFit: A horse used to carry burdens is a drudge and is literally loaded with packs.

clue.text: Ah! Ballet or rally possibly seen here?

definitions.text: Ah! Ballet or rally possibly seen here?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged into another form

explanation.surface: A concert-goer exclaims at the range of events a famous venue hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the fifteen letters of AH BALLET OR RALLY; the whole clue also defines, since ballets and rallies are both staged at the London concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed London concert hall in Kensington hosts ballet, concerts and political rallies, so such events are seen there.

clue.text: Regular hospital attendant

definitions.meaning: a hospital worker who carries out non-medical tasks for patients

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tidy and methodical, and the noun is a hospital's ancillary attendant.

clue.text: Chemical found in chalk a little?

indicators.note: the answer is found in the letters of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A chemist wonders whether a little of some substance turns up in chalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals that the answer sits inside 'chalk a little', from the H onwards; the question mark admits that chalk itself is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: A soluble base such as soda or potash is a class of chemical compound, so the general word defines it.

clue.text: Leaves smoky taste when served from China?

definitions.text: Leaves smoky taste when served from China?

parts.words: Leaves smoky taste when served from China?
parts.note: read as a dish that leaves a smoky aftertaste, but the leaves are tea leaves with a smoky flavour, from the country and served in fine porcelain cups

explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese black tea is dried over pine fires, giving its leaves a smoky taste.

clue.text: Distribute the books to everyone

parts.note: all means everyone
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A librarian is told to hand out the books to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests handing out library books; 'to' only means 'attached to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute shares or portions among people.

clue.text: Introduced fancy set in red

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A jeweller presents an ornate setting picked out in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the eight letters of SET IN RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to put or introduce something into another thing, so the past tense means introduced.

clue.text: Series about the river a long runner?

indicators.note: the series abbreviation goes about the river, enclosing it

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A run of television episodes about a river turns out to be a long-running show.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the runner is a horse or athlete with stamina, not a long-running series; the Tay is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a racehorse or athlete with stamina for long distances, so it is a long-distance runner.

clue.text: Unreliable amateur repair work round the church

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, so the work encloses the church

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home repair work done by amateurs
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Home handymen botching jobs around the parish church can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY, short for do-it-yourself, is the British term for home repairs done by amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicey is informal British for risky or uncertain, so it means unreliable.

clue.text: Modify (adapt) elms to become bearers of fruit

indicators.note: to modify something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to change some elm trees so that they start yielding fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket around 'adapt' makes it look like a gloss on 'Modify', but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These palm trees produce the sweet fruit of the Middle East, so they are bearers of fruit.

clue.text: Shrewd about choral working, showing great knowledge

indicators.note: the shrewd word goes about the rearranged one, enclosing it

parts.note: shrewd means sly, cunning

indicators.note: working on something reshapes it, so the letters of choral are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever singer, cunning about choral work, displays deep learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the choral letters into CHOLAR before the shrewd word wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned, academic person is one who displays great knowledge, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Teacher losing head makes bloomer

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher, master for short

explanation.surface: A headless schoolmaster makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder in the surface but is the definition in its other sense: something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A Michaelmas daisy is a garden flower, and a flower is crossword shorthand for a bloomer, a thing that blooms.

clue.text: A novel piece of headwear

definitions.meaning: the 1894 novel by George du Maurier featuring the hypnotist Svengali
a soft felt hat with an indented crown

explanation.definitionFit: The felt hat took its name from the title heroine of du Maurier's novel, so one word serves both senses.

clue.text: Reassess level of study about old king (English)

indicators.note: the study word goes about the king, holding him inside

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: An examiner reconsiders the standard of a course concerning an old English king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level of study' looks like one phrase (a grade) but splits after 'level'; to read a subject is British for studying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something's level is to place it in a new grade, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Reform — the last word with millions in depression

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

indicators.note: the millions letter goes in the depression word

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Reformers say finance has the final say, with millions lost in the slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Amen closes a prayer, which is why it is 'the last word'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to improve a law or text, a reform.

clue.text: Fellow to go wrong in business transaction delay

indicators.note: the fellow and the error go inside the business word

parts.note: a deal is a business transaction
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A colleague slips up during a business deal, holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'delay' as a hold-up in a deal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferral is a postponement, the putting off of something until later, so a delay.

clue.text: It's always established as the highest

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
EST is the usual abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A claim that something has always been recognised as supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak is the world's tallest mountain, so it is the highest.

clue.text: Turn up this to bring about happy ending

definitions.text: Turn up this to bring about happy ending

parts.words: Turn up this to bring about happy ending
parts.note: the idiom of things working out well by 'turning up' the winning cards of the leading suit in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: In card games these are the winning suit, and to turn them up is to end well unexpectedly.

clue.text: Food supplier has more than most fat, we hear

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like another word with a different spelling

parts.note: grosser means fatter, more obese than others

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper selling food is fatter than most people, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that GROSSER (fatter) said out loud sounds like the shopkeeper's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling foodstuffs and household goods, so a supplier of food.

clue.text: Gate I do up — seen in the garden

definitions.text: Gate I do up — seen in the garden

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener fixes the gate, and the result can be seen in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges GATE I DO; the whole clue also defines, since the flower grows in gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is an annual garden flower with satiny pink and white blooms, seen in gardens.

clue.text: Press man at the top

parts.note: read as someone on a press or at the top of a stack, but it means the journalist in charge of a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper decides its content, so he is the top man of the press.

clue.text: Order to work when 21 around clubs

indicators.note: the work word goes around the card suit, enclosing it

parts.note: 21 down is a press man at the top; his work is to edit copy
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief, working at cards, is told to get on with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside EDIT. The cross-reference sends you to 21-down, and what that man does at work is edit.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree, which is a formal order issued by authority.

clue.text: State (not North America) in the country

indicators.note: not means the named letters are left out of the state word

parts.note: Indiana is a US state

explanation.surface: A visitor states they are not in North America but in another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes NA from INDIANA. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The country of south Asia with the capital New Delhi, the world's most populous nation.

clue.text: Sudden changes about beginning of month leaving sun unsettled

annotationWithheld.clue: Sudden changes about beginning of month leaving sun unsettled

clue.text: VIP treatment that's laid down

parts.note: special treatment for an important guest, read as the actual crimson floor covering unrolled for them to walk on

explanation.definitionFit: A crimson strip of floor covering is unrolled for dignitaries, so the phrase means lavish welcome.

clue.text: Open the deliveries on time

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator says the bowling is unguarded and right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden, so it is a synonym of open.

clue.text: Likely to fit after hat's diameter taken

indicators.note: the fit word comes after the trimmed hat word
the diameter's letter is taken away from the hat word

parts.note: lid is informal for a hat
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A hatter thinks it will probably fit once the hat's width has been measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is slang for a hat, and D is the usual abbreviation for diameter in formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable to do something means being likely or apt to do it, as in 'liable to break'.

clue.text: Leader of navvies holds good man to be a crook

indicators.note: the foreman word holds the saint inside it

parts.note: a ganger is the foreman in charge of a gang of labourers, navvies being British road and rail labourers
ST, saint, is the crossword's usual good man

explanation.surface: A foreman of labourers shelters a decent fellow who turns out to be a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of navvies' looks like a first-letter instruction (N) but is a whole word: the foreman of a labouring gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a criminal gang, so he is a crook.
